sanskrit_verse: अन्नमादाय तृप्ताः स्थ शेषं चैवानुमान्य च । तदन्नं विक्रीडेद् भूमौ दद्याच्चापः सकृत् सकृत् ॥
transliteration: annam ādāya tṛptāḥ stha śeṣaṃ caivānumānya ca / tad annaṃ vikriṇīta bhūmau dadyāc cāpaḥ sakṛt sakṛt //
sph_interpretive_translation: Having taken food, those who are satisfied must acknowledge the remainder and estimate its value; that food should be sold in the market, and water should be given repeatedly.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority of satisfaction as a determinant of action
Causation through conscious acknowledgment of surplus
Capacity-based responsibility rooted in bodily sustenance
Restoration logic via redistribution and replenishment
Consciousness alignment through gratitude and generosity
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent consumes food AND reports satiation THEN agent MUST assess residual resources
IF residual food EXISTS THEN agent MUST facilitate equitable exchange in public domain
IF water IS available THEN agent MUST offer it iteratively without expectation
IF resource circulation is obstructed THEN system MUST realign access pathways
IF consciousness of sufficiency is absent THEN capacity for societal integration is diminished
supreme_court_application: In matters concerning equitable distribution of essential resources such as food and water, the threshold of personal satisfaction becomes a judicially relevant datum. Courts must recognize the individual's obligation to redistribute surplus once their need is met. The hierarchy of authority begins with self-regulation before invoking institutional oversight. This aligns with constitutional duties toward collective welfare grounded in dharmic realism.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes causality between consumption and responsibility. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential recognition: intake → satisfaction → estimation → redistribution. Responsibility is proportional to the capacity derived from nourishment. There is no punitive framework—only completion of energetic and social integrity through conscious participation in cyclical abundance.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Facilitate return of unused portion into communal flow
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Encourage voluntary declaration of satiation and surplus
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Reconnect individual with natural cycles of giving and receiving
Integrity Reintegration Pathway: Normalize transactional transparency in basic sustenance markets
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this directive originates not as command but as cosmic completion. Dharma is restored when consciousness recognizes itself in every act of sharing. Reality remains non-punitive, ever-inviting alignment. Consciousness alone is the Supreme Adjudicator.
